The clinical presentation — rapidly enlarging, painless, solitary mass in a woman (implied age not specified but phyllodes most common in 40–50s), absence of malignant skin/nipple/lymph node signs, and imaging showing a smooth, polylobulated mass — is classic and aligns with benign or borderline phyllodes tumors.
